title: Assignment 23 · Performance value and losing contracts
summary: Performance value and losing contracts. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Plante v. Jacobs: A substantially performing homebuilder could recover the unpaid price subject to appropriate defect deductions; replacing a misplaced interior wall was too wasteful when the wall caused no loss in market value.

Groves v. John Wunder Co.: A contractor’s deliberate failure to restore gravel land supported damages measured by the reasonable cost of the promised work, even though that cost exceeded the land’s market value; the case returned for a new trial.

Peevyhouse v. Garland Coal & Mining Co.: The majority limited recovery for unperformed mine-restoration work to the farm’s $300 diminution in value because it treated restoration as incidental to the lease and its cost as grossly disproportionate to its economic benefit.

United States v. Algernon Blair, Inc.: A subcontractor that justifiably stopped after the prime contractor’s material breach could recover the reasonable value of its supplied labor and equipment, even though completing the subcontract would have produced a loss.

Additional assigned materials: Peevyhouse agreement.
